title: UiNode
description: The declared UI schema (platform plan 6.2): a page is a tree of these nodes, rendered natively by React (web shell, PWA) today and by SwiftUI (iPhone, Apple TV) later. Session B step 5 adds List, CardGrid, MediaShelf, DetailPane and SplitView (platform plan 6.2's named generic primitives) alongside v0's Chat-only set; see docs/dev.md's 'A2UI' entry for exactly which pages this session converted to real schema pages and which stayed hand-written React, and why.

source.description: route: the app's own backend route. host: a host.* RPC method (4.9). package: a data call of the package whose page this is (APP-KIND-01); `path` is then a `contributes.data[]` id, never a URL, and the call is POST /api/plugins/<package id>/data/<path>.

stream.description: True when this binding delivers incremental updates (turn.token during a Chat reply, 7.2) rather than one value.

params.description: Source "package" only: the JSON body of the data call. Each value is a literal or the string "$state.<name>", read from page state at call time (a picker writes it). A value that is an object with numeric `lat` and `lon` (Current location) travels in the body only and is never part of a query key, URL, log or cache.

package_binding.description: A binding whose source is "package": the nodes that draw a package's own data (answer_blocks, picker) take only this.

state.description: NEWS-00: a literal map written into the target page's state on arrival (a channel page reads its `kind` and `key` this way). String values may contain `{field}` placeholders, resolved from the bound list item or card the action fires for (as `call.args` do); a value is never read from another page's state.

target.description: A route or host.* method. May contain a `{field}` placeholder (a bound list item's own field, substituted per item/per selected item by a list's row_action or batch action).

args.description: String values may contain `{field}` placeholders, resolved the same way as `target`.

fresh_confirm.description: Before the call, the host asks for a fresh secret for this row's id. A returned ticket is merged into the row as `{ticket}` for args templating. The kit draws no dialog.

success_label.description: QA-FINISH-01: after the call succeeds, the kit shows this text as a brief toast ("Saved"). May contain `{field}` placeholders. Absent: no toast. A failed call shows its error instead.

then.description: MUSIC-LIKE-01: after the call succeeds, go to a page. The JSON object the call answers with is merged over the item, so `{band_id}` in `navigate.to` or `navigate.state` reads the answer's own field. A failed call goes nowhere and shows its error. Navigation only: a call never chains into another call.

play.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: hand a media item to the host's player (the shell's audio session). `media_id` may contain `{field}` placeholders, resolved from the bound item the action fires for (`{id}`). The page never plays anything itself; a host with no player refuses the action with a message.

position_s.description: The start position in seconds. String values may contain `{field}` placeholders resolved from the bound item.

share.description: PARITY-01: share a link to a page of this hub. `to` is a route inside the hub (starting with `/`, `{field}` placeholders allowed); the kit builds the full hub address, hands it to the device share sheet when there is one, and otherwise copies it. Nothing is sent to any service.

title.description: Optional share title; may contain `{field}` placeholders.

prompt.description: May contain `{field}`/`{count}` placeholders, resolved against the same item(s) `on_confirm` will act on.

status.description: MEDIA-PARITY-02: a status slot inside the dialog. The binding reads one status-card row ({state, title, detail}, as the S6 health rows); the dialog draws it as a card above its buttons, so a failed confirm shows its error in place instead of closing. Omitted: no card, as before. (Dialogs are declared only as `confirm`; no separate dialog node exists.)

action.description: Exactly one of the declared actions (6.2). PARITY-01: row-menu operations need no new op. Play next, Add to queue, Mark played and Unfollow are a `call` to the package route with the row in `args`; Go to artist or album is a `navigate`; Share is `share`.

share_change.description: The host's calls for changing who can see the created item. Each call receives the bound creation row, with person_id added for add and remove.

creation_header_data.description: The row returned by a creation_header bind. Display fields may be null or omitted; the kit supplies plain fallback labels. creator.href is a host-owned router destination and link_label optionally replaces the default accessible name.

label.description: Plain creator fallback, usually Made at home.

href.description: Optional host router destination. When present, the avatar and name are one link.

link_label.description: Optional accessible name for the creator link; defaults to '<name>, open profile'.

candidates.description: Optional list used by the share panel when no separate candidates_bind is set.

creation_header.description: The shared creation identity and visibility pattern. `bind` returns one `creation_header_data` row (or an array whose first row is used). `candidates_bind`, when present, returns candidate people; otherwise row.candidates is used. A creator href is a host-owned route; when present the avatar and name form one router link. Missing names fall back to plain labels; a raw template token is never shown.

candidates_bind.description: Optional binding returning candidate people [{id, name, avatar_url?}] for the share panel.

variant.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-03 (K2): `studio` is a page header: the optional `eyebrow` as a small uppercase tracked line, the row's title as a huge bold uppercase heading, the row's art (`fields.art`) at the start, and `secondary` then `primary` at the end. It draws no creator line, date, description or visibility chip. Default `full`, unchanged.

backdrop.description: PARITY-01: `art_gradient` draws a soft static gradient behind the header, taken from the dominant colour of the row's art (`fields.art`), falling back to the theme tokens when the art is missing or cannot be read. Default `none`, unchanged.

eyebrow.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-03 (K2): `studio` variant only. The line above the title (CREATE, STUDIO), drawn uppercase.

locked.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-03 (K2): `studio` variant only. Dotted path to a boolean in the row; true draws no art, eyebrow or title (an adult-only item while the lock is on). The actions stay.

secondary.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-03 (K2): `studio` variant only. A quiet pill drawn before `primary` (at most one primary).

icon.description: MUSIC-POLISH-01: an icon name from the kit set. Default "shuffle".

labeled.description: MUSIC-POLISH-01: draw the label beside the icon, not an icon alone (an Artist's Start radio).

tone.description: Deprecated: ignored; every page follows the selected theme

surface.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-02: the surface the page body draws on. `page` (default) is unchanged. `studio` draws the body as a rounded pane (full bleed on a phone) carrying `data-surface="studio"`, which sets the kit's studio token scope: near-black neutrals and a lime primary in dark whatever the selected look, a soft grey page, white cards and a deeper lime in light. Tokens only; a colour never comes from the page.

condition.description: A simple expression string evaluated against page state; absent means always shown.

message_thread.description: The Chat pattern component (6.2 names Chat as one of the three hardest pages to express; this is the pattern component that resulted, not one of the plan's named generic primitives). Session B step 4 rebuilt Chat on @assistant-ui/react, which owns its own history loading, streaming, thread list and message actions entirely inside React (chatModelAdapter.ts, chatThreadListAdapter.ts) - v0's bind/sender_field/text_field described a generic turn-list interpreter never built (see git history on this file); this node is now just a mount point, the same role `settings_editor` plays for Settings.

settings_editor.description: Mounts the kit's own settings renderer (frontend/src/kit/settings/SettingsRenderer.tsx), which already reads the settings registry generically (docs/SETTINGS.md's 'one definition, the generic renderer') - a second, JSON-authored description of the same data would be a competing source of truth, not a schema page in the sense the other nodes here are. Session B step 7 ('settings as an editor') extends that renderer directly (a tree sidebar, search, scope tabs); this node's own shape never changes.

action_label.description: The button's words for the action (for example "Add a folder"). Without it the kit derives a plain label from the action kind.

secondary_action.description: A second way forward, drawn as a quiet button beside the first. Only drawn when `action` is set.

secondary_action_label.description: The second button's words (for example "Upload a picture"). Without it the kit derives a plain label from the action kind.

scope.description: selected: the interpreter loops `action` once per currently-selected item, substituting `{field}` placeholders from that item. all: loops over every currently-loaded item regardless of selection (docs/BACKLOG.md's 'clear-all where the whole list is disposable').

list.description: The kit's List primitive (frontend/src/kit/primitives/List.tsx), bound to one route that returns an array. Content-agnostic like the primitive it wraps: a row shows item_label_field as its title and, when given, item_subtitle_field/item_badge_field underneath - a single-line-per-field template, not a full custom renderItem (a page needing richer per-row layout than that stays hand-written React; docs/plans/session-b-ui.md step 5's recorded decision on People and Privacy).

item_subtitle_field.description: A `{field}` template string (the same substitution as action.call's target/args), not a bare dotted path - lets a row's subtitle combine more than one field ('{category} · {scope}') without a richer per-row template mechanism.

item_badge_field.description: Dotted path to a boolean; true shows a small badge (item_badge_label) next to the subtitle.

hide_when_empty.description: QA-FINISH-01: draw nothing (not even the empty text) when the bound call returns no rows, so a list with nothing in it is simply absent. A load error still shows.

item_media_field.description: NEWS-00: dotted path to a lucide icon name or a same-origin image path (starting with `/`); drawn as the row's leading media. An address with a scheme or host is refused, so a row never loads another site's picture.

row_toggle.description: NEWS-00: a per-row switch (Follow, Save). `field` is the dotted path to a boolean on the row; the action is fired with the row's fields and `on` set to the new value.

card_grid.description: The kit's CardGrid primitive (frontend/src/kit/primitives/CardGrid.tsx). No page uses this yet (platform plan 6.2: Videos/Music, not in this session's scope) - added now for catalog/schema completeness (docs/plans/session-b-ui.md step 5's own agreement test), same minimal single-field-per-card shape as `list`.

media_shelf.description: The kit's MediaShelf primitive (ui/src/primitives/MediaShelf.tsx): a sideways rail of media tiles at one declared aspect (wide 16:9, poster 2:3, square 1:1). MEDIA-PLAYER-01 adds the heading, a caption subtitle, the played-share bar, a corner badge and a running-time label; on a package page `on_select` may be a `play` action.

heading.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: the shelf's heading ("Continue watching"), which also names the rail.

heading_style.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-03 (K5): `eyebrow` draws the heading, and the day group labels, as a small uppercase tracked line in the muted text colour. Default `default`, unchanged.

item_subtitle_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: a `{field}` template for the caption's second line (the channel, the artist), as list.item_subtitle_field.

item_media_field.description: Dotted path to the tile's same-origin image path (starting with `/`). An address with a scheme or a host is not loaded.

item_progress_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: dotted path to the played share, a number 0 to 1, drawn as a bar along the tile's bottom edge.

item_avatar_field.description: PARITY-01: dotted path to a same-origin image path (starting with `/`) drawn as a small round avatar (channel, artist) beside the caption. Empty draws none.

item_badge_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: dotted path to a short string drawn as the tile's corner badge ("Saved", "On this phone", "Not saved"); empty draws none.

item_badge_presentation.description: MEDIA-PARITY-02: `dot` draws `item_badge_field` as a small unplayed dot on the tile (shown when the field is truthy, with the field's string as its accessible name when it is one) instead of a corner label. Default `label`, unchanged.

item_meta_field.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: dotted path to the running time, a number of seconds (drawn as 18:42) or a short string.

look.description: VIDEO-LD-01: backdrop fills the art box with a softly blurred copy of its image and contains the sharp image over it. Default default.

variant.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: card draws the shelf inside a bordered section card; plain draws a frameless row (a heading, the optional See all link, then the tiles), as the media apps and News do.

orientation.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: horizontal is the sideways rail; vertical stacks the tiles as rows, the picture at the start and the caption beside it (Up next beside a player).

layout.description: Grid wraps whole tiles from the existing card-size budget, with two columns on a phone. Vertical orientation takes precedence.

art_shape.description: Circle uses square artwork clipped to a circle, including its current ring.

density.description: Compact vertical rows have 72 px artwork, two caption lines and trailing item_meta_field running time. Horizontal shelves use the existing card-size budget.

item_highlight_field.description: Dotted path to a boolean; true marks the current track or next episode with the media current ring token and aria-current.

item_index_field.description: Dotted path to the leading track index in a vertical row; zero is displayed.

sort.description: PARITY-01: a sort control above the shelf (Recents, A to Z, Creator). The chosen option's `value` is written to page state `state`; put `$state.<state>` in the bind params so the backend sorts. The first option is the default.

chips.description: PARITY-01: a filter chip row above the shelf, one chip chosen at a time (Songs, Albums). The chosen `value` is written to page state `state`; the first option is the default and normally means All. Put `$state.<state>` in the bind params so the backend filters.

pinned_field.description: PARITY-01: dotted path to a boolean on each row; rows where it is true are drawn first in a Pinned row, then the rest. At most `pinned_max` pins are drawn.

pinned_max.description: PARITY-01: how many pinned rows are drawn.

pinned_heading.description: PARITY-01: the Pinned row's heading. Default: Pinned.

row_actions.description: Vertical row controls outside the artwork button. Play is icon-only; other actions are labelled pills. Labels may contain {field} placeholders; a nonempty label_field value overrides the label. Each action receives its row, just like on_select.

show_when_field.description: Draw this button only when this row field is truthy.

hide_when_field.description: Draw this button only when this row field is falsy.

card_radius.description: PRO-LOOK-01 (section 17): soft draws the tiles with the 18 pt soft card radius. MUSIC-KIT-01: tight draws the tiles with the 8 px media card radius token (the modern music look). Round art (art_shape circle) stays round.

press_scale.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: a tile shrinks slightly while pressed. Gated on reduced motion by the kit.

on_play.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: draws a round Play button over each tile on hover or focus (never on touch screens). It fires this action with the tile's row, the same as a `play` on_select. Horizontal shelves only.

play_label.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: a `{field}` template for the Play button's accessible name ("Play {title}"). Default: the tile's label.

hide_when_empty.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: draw nothing (no heading, no empty state) when the bound call returns no rows, so a shelf with nothing in it is simply absent. A load error still shows.

see_all.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: a link beside the heading ("See all"), usually a `navigate` to the app's full list. Fired with no row.

group_by_field.description: VIDEO-UI-05 (K12): dotted path to a date (an ISO string, or epoch seconds or milliseconds). Grid layout only: rows are grouped by local calendar day, in the order the call returns them, and each group opens with the kit's DayDivider, a centred label between hairlines ("Today, 5 clips", "Yesterday, 2 clips", then "Mon, Oct 27, 3 clips"). A row with no readable date joins the group before it. Absent: one ungrouped grid.

group_noun.description: VIDEO-UI-05 (K12): the word counted in each day heading (one: "clip", other: "clips"). Absent: "item" and "items".

size_control.description: VIDEO-UI-05 (K12): draws the kit's CardSizeSlider above a grid layout; the slider sets the tile size (the shared --maipai-card-size) and is remembered per device. A phone keeps two columns.

locked_field.description: ADULT-LOCK-01: dotted path to a boolean on each row (default `locked`). A row where it is true is a locked item: the kit drops it before reading any other field and the shelf draws ONE identical lock tile after the open items, whatever their number. The host's redacted row is `{ locked: true, making?: boolean }` and nothing else; the tile has no title, description, picture, tags or count. Pressing it opens the page's passcode dialog (the kit `AdultLockProvider`).

making_field.description: ADULT-LOCK-01: dotted path to a boolean (default `making`) on a locked row: a locked item is still being made, so the one tile shows a small spinner and nothing else.

favorite.description: VIDEO-UI-05 (K12): a heart toggle on each tile. `field` is the dotted path to the row's boolean (true draws a filled heart); a press flips it at once and fires `action` with the row, its `field` set to the new value, so the call can send it. A failed call puts the heart back and says so.

media_loop.description: VIDEO-UI-14 (item 8): a tile plays a muted, looped clip over its poster (`item_media_field`, still an image). The clip's same-origin path is read from `item_loop_field`. It plays while the tile is in view, is paused off screen, and under reduced motion only the poster shows. A row with no readable clip shows its poster alone. Rail and grid layouts.

item_loop_field.description: VIDEO-UI-14: dotted path to the same-origin path of a short silent mp4 (starting with `/`) that `media_loop` plays over the poster. Required when `media_loop` is true.

reorder.description: MEDIA-PARITY-02: rows can be reordered. Each row shows a drag handle and keyboard move controls (Move up, Move down). After a move the kit fires `call` once with the complete new order as an array of row keys (`item_key_field`) under the name `id_param` in the call's body, then keeps the new order if the call succeeds and puts the old order back with a plain notice if it fails.

id_param.description: The body field that carries the ordered key array (for example `ids`).

quick_tiles.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: the kit's QuickTiles block (ui/src/primitives/MusicBlocks.tsx): Listen now's "Pick up where you left off", a two-column (three from 768 px) grid of compact tiles, small square art beside a title. A tile selects with `on_select`; `on_play` adds a round Play button on hover or focus (never on touch screens) that fires with the same row.

item_media_field.description: Dotted path to the art's same-origin image path (starting with `/`).

max.description: At most this many tiles are drawn.

play_label.description: A `{field}` template for the Play button's accessible name ("Play {title}").

hide_when_empty.description: Draw nothing when the bound call returns no rows.

top_result.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: the kit's TopResultCard block: Search's Top result, a large card with art, an eyebrow ("Artist"), the name, one quiet line and an always-visible round Play button. The bound call returns rows; the first row is used.

item_eyebrow_field.description: A `{field}` template for the small line above the title.

item_subtitle_field.description: A `{field}` template for the quiet line under the title.

item_media_field.description: Dotted path to the art's same-origin image path.

play_label.description: A `{field}` template for the Play button's accessible name ("Play {title}").

hide_when_empty.description: Draw nothing when the bound call returns no rows.

category_tiles.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: the kit's CategoryTiles block: Search's empty state, colour tiles for genre, mood, decade and "Made here". The tile mixes its colour into the card colour so the title keeps its contrast in light and dark.

item_color_field.description: Dotted path to a colour string (#rgb, #rrggbb, or an rgb(), hsl() or oklch() function). Anything else is ignored and the tile keeps the neutral colour.

item_media_field.description: Dotted path to optional art tucked into the tile's corner (same-origin path).

hide_when_empty.description: Draw nothing when the bound call returns no rows.

track_rows.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: the kit's TrackRows block: Album and Playlist tracklists. Each row has a number (it turns into a play icon on hover or focus), a title and artist, and an end label. Pressing the number or the row plays it through `on_play`, with the row. Play counts are data: a page for a child profile binds rows that carry no count field, so no count is drawn.

item_subtitle_field.description: A `{field}` template for the artist line.

item_number_field.description: Dotted path to the number shown at the row's start. Default: the 1-based position.

item_meta_field.description: Dotted path to the end label: a number of seconds (drawn as 3:42) or a short string such as a play count. A row without it draws none.

item_group_field.description: Dotted path to a heading drawn before each run of equal values (a disc: "Disc 2").

item_highlight_field.description: Dotted path to a boolean; true marks the playing row.

play_label.description: A `{field}` template for the Play button's accessible name ("Play {title}").

row_actions.description: MUSIC-POLISH-01: quiet icon buttons at each row's end (a Playlist's Remove x), faint until the row is hovered or focused. Each action receives its row, as on_play does. Labels may contain {field} placeholders.

reorder.description: MEDIA-PARITY-02: rows can be reordered. Each row shows a drag handle and keyboard move controls (Move up, Move down). After a move the kit fires `call` once with the complete new order as an array of row keys (`item_key_field`) under the name `id_param` in the call's body, then keeps the new order if the call succeeds and puts the old order back with a plain notice if it fails.

id_param.description: The body field that carries the ordered key array (for example `ids`).

hide_when_empty.description: Draw nothing when the bound call returns no rows.

result_feed.description: VIDEO-UI-04 (K9, K10): the kit's ResultFeed block, a newest-first feed of the package's own rows. Each row is one entry: its words, tags, reference chips (a Start frame chip with its thumbnail), one `VideoPlayer` (queued, generating, draft, ready, failed, cancelled) and its actions. `filters` write page state that `bind.params` reads as `$state.<name>`. Entries are grouped under a `DayDivider` per day of `fields.created_at` (or, while a toggle marked `group` is on, under their words). The player's built-in Stop, Try again, Make another, Render, Another still, Edit words and Favorite are mapped from `handlers`; only extra buttons (Remix, Make it Max) are `actions`. `starts` on a handler or action marks it as starting a picture or video: the host's `makingNotice` disables it with that notice. `poll_while` is required: the feed re-reads only the running rows' own records, every `FEED_POLL_INTERVAL_MS` (3 s, defined once in ui/src/schema/feedPolling.ts) while any row's status is one of `poll_while.statuses`, stops when none is, and re-reads at once when a hidden tab is shown again.

fields.description: Dotted paths into each row. `key` defaults to "id".

tags.description: Dotted path to an array of short strings.

references.description: Dotted path to an array of {label, thumb}; thumb is a same-origin path.

status.description: Dotted path to one of queued, generating, draft, ready, failed, cancelled.

progress.description: Dotted path to 0 to 100, or null.

started_at.description: Dotted path to epoch milliseconds the job started.

poster.description: Dotted path to the still (a draft's picture, a clip's poster).

src.description: Dotted path to the clip's same-origin path.

created_at.description: Dotted path to an ISO date or epoch milliseconds; the day headings read it.

locked.description: ADULT-LOCK-01: dotted path to a boolean (default `locked`). A row where it is true is a locked clip: the feed draws ONE identical lock tile after the open entries, whatever their number, and reads no other field of the row (no words, tags, picture or count).

making.description: ADULT-LOCK-01: dotted path to a boolean (default `making`) on a locked row: a locked clip is still being made, so the one tile shows a small spinner and nothing else.

options.description: A select's choices; the first is the default.

group.description: A toggle only: while on, entries with the same words are gathered under a heading of those words, in place of the day headings.

handlers.description: The VideoPlayer's own built-in actions, each one action run with the row. `starts` is the K8 marker.

actions.description: Extra buttons after the built-in ones. With no `when`, an action shows in `ready`.

show_when.description: Dotted row-field path; truthy shows this action, falsy or missing hides it.

actions_variant.description: Passed to each VideoPlayer; `icons` needs VIDEO-UI-02's player.

actions_inline.description: Passed to each VideoPlayer; the rest go in its More menu (VIDEO-UI-02).

look.description: VIDEO-UI-14 (item 2): `media` draws the feed picture first: the newest entry wide and the rest in a grid (two columns only while the feed's own pane gives each at least 320 px, one otherwise), the entry's tags drawn on the picture's top edge, the words shown once under it, and the player's icon row over the picture, shown on hover or keyboard focus and always on touch. A running, failed or stopped entry keeps its progress, Stop, reason and Try again visible. `default` is the single column with the words above the player.

heading_style.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-03 (K5): `eyebrow` draws the day headings, and the filter labels, as a small uppercase tracked line in the muted text colour. Default `default`, unchanged.

filters_presentation.description: VIDEO-UI-14 (item 6): `popover` puts the same filter controls behind one View button (a popover, a sheet on a phone); `inline` draws them in a row above the feed.

statuses.description: The statuses that mean a job is running. Every other status is settled.

record.description: The read of one job's own record: a data call of this package (a `contributes.data[]` id), POSTed with `params` filled from the running row (`{id}`); it returns that row in the feed's shape.

image_editor.description: IMG-STUDIO-01: the kit's ImageEditor as a page block, the picture Studio. `bind` reads ONE picture row, chosen from the page state by a Library file id (for example `bind.params: { id: "$state.file" }`): `{ id, title, url, width, height, locked, versions: [{ id, url, label, created_at, width, height }] }`, versions oldest first with the original first; without `versions` the row's own `url` is the one version. The Element draws the tools Markup, Comment, Remove BG, Erase, Resize, Crop (drag handles, Free, Original, 1:1, 4:5, 16:9 and 9:16, rotate left and right, flip horizontal and vertical), Adjust (brightness, contrast, saturation, warmth, Auto) and Compare (before and after the first version), and a More tool listing `operations`. Every result is a preview the person Applies (a NEW version) or Undoes; nothing is overwritten. A row whose `fields.locked` path is true draws ONE lock tile and reads no other field. `handlers.apply` and `handlers.markup` replies may also carry `locked: true` (and an optional `note`): the new version was saved behind the person's lock, so the Element keeps showing the picture being edited and says so in one plain line. All I/O goes through `handlers`; each is a `call` whose own `args` name the placeholders it wants from the values listed here (a whole placeholder such as `{args}` or `{region}` keeps its JSON type, as in `studio`); a handler with no entry disables its tool with its `tool_reasons` line (a tool never disappears). `handlers.run` is a `call` run with `{ file, operation, args }` where `operation` is `crop` (args `x`, `y`, `width`, `height` as fractions of the rotated and flipped picture, `aspect`, `rotate` 0, 90, 180 or 270, `flip_horizontal`, `flip_vertical`), `adjust` (args `brightness`, `contrast`, `saturation`, `warmth` each -100 to 100, `auto`), `remove_background`, `erase` (args `mask`, a PNG data URL), `upscale` (args `scale`), `resize` (args `width`, `height`) or the `id` of one of `operations` (args the values of its controls); its JSON reply is the preview `{ token, preview_url, width, height, transparent }`. `handlers.apply` is a `call` run with `{ file, token, label }` whose reply is the new version `{ id, url, label, width, height }`. `handlers.markup` is a `call` run with `{ file, png }` (a PNG data URL) with the same reply. `handlers.comment` is a `call` run with `{ file, prompt, region, mask, reference }` (`region` `{ x, y, width, height }` fractions or null; `mask` a PNG data URL or null; `reference` `{ id, label }` or null) whose reply is `{ message, preview }` where `preview` is optional and shaped like the run reply. `handlers.pick_reference` is a `call` whose reply is `{ id, label }` or null (the host's Library picker). The page state is not written; after Apply the bound row is read again and the new version is shown.

fields.description: Dotted paths into the bound row. Defaults are the names in the node description.

locked.description: Dotted path to a boolean (default `locked`). True draws the one lock tile and reads no other field.

empty.description: Dotted path to a boolean (default `empty`). True marks the row as a placeholder (there is no picture to open and nothing to pick): the node draws `empty_state` and reads no other field.

empty_state.description: Drawn instead of the default line when the row is a placeholder (`fields.empty`). A page that has its own picker uses it for the case where the picker has nothing either.

hide_when_empty.description: Draw nothing when the bound data has no row (the page's picker is shown instead). A placeholder row still draws `empty_state`.

initial_tool.description: The tool open at first (for example `crop` from a Crop button). A tool that is not listed, or is disabled, is ignored.

tools.description: Which tools are on. A tool of the five chat tools (markup, comment, remove_background, erase, resize) that is not listed is drawn disabled ("Not offered here."), never removed; `crop`, `adjust` and `more` are drawn only when listed. Default: all of them (`more` only when `operations` has rows).

tool_reasons.description: A plain line that disables a tool and is shown as its tooltip and in the status line (for example while the picture engine is not ready). A tool with no reason is enabled when its handler exists.

compare.description: Draw Compare. Disabled, with its reason, while the current picture is the original.

comment_brush.description: Comment gains Brush (a painted area sent as `mask`).

resize_upscale.description: Draw the Resize bar's own Upscale 2x and 4x buttons. False when the host offers Make clearer instead.

operations.description: The extra one-click operations, read from the host's registry, drawn under More. The Element names none of them. Each row: `{ id, label, summary, controls, enabled, reason }`; `controls` is a list of `{ kind: "number", name, label, min, max, step, default }` or `{ kind: "choice", name, label, options, default }`. A row with `enabled` false is drawn disabled with its `reason` as the tooltip. EDITOR-TOOLS-READY: a row with `tool` (one of markup, comment, remove_background, erase, resize, crop, adjust) is not an operation: it is the readiness of that built-in tool, `{ tool, enabled, reason }`. A tool whose row says `enabled` false is drawn disabled from the start and its `reason` is shown as the editor's one line before any click (the host's own not-ready line when the row has none). It is never listed under More.

add_picture.description: EDITOR-AGE-ADD: an "Add a picture" control for a page whose editor has no picture open. It opens the host's own media picker (the person's Library pictures, or an upload through the Library's own route with its gates); the chosen file's id is given to `action` as `{id}` (usually a `navigate` that writes it to the page state). It is drawn as the main action of the placeholder row's empty state (the empty state's own action moves to the second place) and as a button under the page's picker, which is where `hide_when_empty` otherwise draws nothing. A host with no picker draws it disabled with the reason.

actions.description: EDITOR-HANDOFF: the page's own hand-offs for the picture on screen, drawn as quiet buttons in the editor's header. Each has a `label` and exactly one of `action` (run with `{file}` set to the Library file id of the version being shown; it stays inside this package like every page action) or `hand_off`. `hand_off: "video_create"` ("Make a video from this") asks the host to open the Video app's Create form with the picture as its start picture: a package page cannot navigate into another app, so the host does it. A hand-off fills a form and starts nothing. A host with no hand-off draws the button disabled with a one-line reason.

pick_reference.description: A `call` run with `{ file, ref }` whose reply is `{ id, label }` (the reference picture checked and named) or null. When the host has a media picker the Element opens it first and `ref` is the Library file id the person chose; without one `ref` is empty and the call chooses for itself. The reply's `id` is sent as `reference` with the next `comment`.

on_close.description: What the editor's Close does (usually a navigate back to the Library).

studio.description: VIDEO-STUDIO-04 and -05 (K3, K4): the kit's TrackStudio block, a timeline editor with a preview. The bound row is one clip: `{ id, title, poster, locked, lanes: [{ id, label, hue, kind, pieces: [{ id, ref, src, label, in_s, out_s, source_s, at_s, level_db, fade_in_s, fade_out_s, crossfade_s, duck }] }] }`; a lane `kind` is video, voice or music. `src` is a same-origin path, or a `blob:` object URL of the page's own origin that the host made from an authenticated read (an adult-only file); the Element never fetches an adult-only file itself. The Element draws the ruler, the lanes (thumbnails and waveforms made inside it), one playhead, the transport (Play, Back to start, Loop, zoom), trim handles, Split at playhead, Delete piece, Add a clip, Add a voice, Add music, Undo and Redo, per-lane Level, Mute and Solo, and the panels Volume, Fades, Crossfade and Level, which act on the selected piece. The preview is client side (one video element as the clock, up to four audio elements, Web Audio gains); nothing is rendered until Export. It cuts where the export dissolves, and says so. A row whose `fields.locked` path is true draws ONE lock tile and nothing else: no media element, no request for a source, no peaks, thumbnails or plan. When the row becomes locked the Element stops every media element, removes `src`, calls `load()` and discards the plan, the peaks and the thumbnails. The plan lives in React state only (no storage, URL or cache). `handlers.export` is one action run with `{ plan, clip }` (whole-placeholder `{plan}` keeps its JSON type); `handlers.add` is a `call` whose JSON reply is the added piece `{ ref, src, label, duration_s }`; a `make_more` item is one action run with `{ clip, piece, at_s }`.

kind.description: `video` draws the monitor and a thumbnail strip on the first lane; `audio` draws no monitor and waveforms only (Music, later).

fields.description: Dotted paths into the bound row. Defaults are the names in the node description.

locked.description: Dotted path to a boolean (default `locked`). True draws the one lock tile and reads no other field.

tools.description: Which Edit buttons are drawn, in this order. Default: all five. Split and Delete piece are built in; the three Add buttons need `handlers.add`, and one without it is not drawn.

tool_reasons.description: A plain line that disables an Add button, shown beside it (for example while a locked item or an engine is not ready). A tool with no reason is enabled.

panels.description: Which right-hand panels are drawn, in this order. Default: all four. Each has a Reset and says which piece or lane it acts on.

audio_pieces.description: Per audio lane. At most four audio elements exist.

level_steps.description: The Level panel's balances. Default is the five of `MIX_LEVELS`: quiet, soft, balanced, loud, very loud.

export_disabled_reason.description: A plain line that disables Export and is shown beside it (for example while the engine cannot take an edit job).

export_result.description: The export job's own card: a bound row drawn by the shipped VideoPlayer in the monitor's place after Export. Polled like `result_feed.poll_while`. When ready it carries `actions` and Keep editing (the plan is kept).

feed_handler.description: VIDEO-UI-04: one action (navigate, call or confirm, exactly one) run with the row, plus the optional K8 `starts` marker (the action starts a picture or a video, so the host's `makingNotice` disables it).

billboard.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: the kit's Billboard block (ui/src/primitives/Billboard.tsx), a rotating hero of bound rows composed from the kit carousel: backdrop art, an eyebrow line, the title, a subtitle, a primary action (Play) and up to two secondary ones. Autoplay pauses on hover, on focus, on a hidden tab and under reduced motion.

size.description: card: a rounded card in the page flow. hero: full width and taller, the title set large (Shows and Films). banner (MEDIA-POLISH-01): a short 340 px band from 640 px, so the first shelf shows under it (Videos); on a phone it grows with its words.

item_eyebrow_field.description: A `{field}` template for the small line over the title.

item_art_field.description: Dotted path to the backdrop's same-origin image path.

hide_when_empty.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: draw nothing when the bound call returns no rows (as media_shelf.hide_when_empty).

billboard_action.description: One Billboard button: its words, an optional lucide icon name, and the action it fires with the slide's row.

player.description: MEDIA-PLAYER-01: the kit's Player (ui/src/primitives/Player.tsx) for one bound media item. The bound call returns the item (an object, or rows whose first row is used). Default field names: id, src, title, subtitle, poster, chapters [{start_s, title}], captions [{src, srclang, label, kind?, default?}], thumbnails (a storyboard WebVTT path), position_s, completed, up_next {id, title, subtitle?, art?}.

layout.description: Default: video for kind video, audio for kind audio.

lyrics_enabled.description: Show the Lyrics control even when the item has no lyrics.

art_spring.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: in the audio layout the cover art grows when playing and settles when paused. Gated on reduced motion by the kit.

lyrics_blur.description: MUSIC-KIT-01: in the audio layout, lyric lines blur and fade by distance from the active line.

lyrics_empty_text.description: Plain empty state shown when lyrics are enabled but the item has no lyrics.

on_lyrics_open.description: Fired once per item the first time Lyrics opens while the row has no lyrics text or timed lines. The row's own fields are the placeholders, such as {id}.

autoplay_next.description: Count down and play up_next when the item ends. Off by default; a child's page leaves it off.

fields.description: Dotted paths that override the default field names.

description.description: Row field containing the optional description; defaults to description.

facts.description: Row field containing the muted facts line; defaults to facts and falls back to subtitle.

lyrics.description: Lyrics text field, default lyrics; reads lyrics.text from a nested lyrics object.

timed_lyrics.description: Timed lyric lines field, default timed_lyrics; reads lyrics.timed from a nested lyrics object.

transcript.description: PARITY-01: field with transcript rows [{start_s, text}]; default transcript.

on_progress.description: Fired every 10 s while playing, on pause, on seek, at the end and on unload. Placeholders: the item's own fields plus {position_s}, {duration_s}, {reason} and {completed}.

on_next.description: Fired with the up_next item's fields (a `play`, or a `navigate` to its watch page).

details.description: MEDIA-DETAIL-01: draw the item's title, facts, expandable description and chapters under the picture (a watch page's details block).

details_show.description: Optional parts of the details block to draw. Absent means title, facts, description and chapters. PARITY-01: `transcript` adds a Transcript button that opens the reader panel (needs `transcript_bind` or the row's transcript field).

rate.description: PODCAST-RATE-01: remembered playback speed. `field` is a dotted row path to a number (the person's saved rate for this show or book) and `value` a constant used when the field is absent or not a number; the field wins. The kit starts at that rate, clamped to its nearest speed option. `on_change` is an action (a `call`) fired when the person picks a speed; placeholders are the item's own fields plus {rate} (a number such as 1.5), so a call body can carry `rate`. Absent: the player starts at 1x and reports nothing.

sleep_timer.description: PARITY-01: draw a sleep timer control (End of episode, 5, 10, 15, 30, 45 or 60 minutes) in the player's extra controls.

skip.description: PARITY-01: skip buttons that jump back and forward by this many seconds (a podcast: 15 and 30).

transcript_bind.description: PARITY-01: the call returning the transcript as rows [{start_s, text}] (or {rows}); the first row of the bound item is not used. Absent: the item's own `transcript` field, if any.

double_tap_seek.description: PARITY-01: video only. A double tap on the left or right third of the picture seeks 10 s back or forward; further quick taps stack.

long_press_speed.description: PARITY-01: video only. Holding the picture plays at 2x until release.

pip.description: PARITY-01: video only. Draw a Picture in picture button (shown only where the browser supports it).

actions_wrap.description: MUSIC-LIKE-02: the actions row wraps onto more lines instead of scrolling sideways with its scrollbar hidden. Use it where the column is narrow or the row has more than three buttons.

actions.description: MEDIA-POLISH-01: the actions row under the title (Like, Watch later, Share to a screen). Each button fires its action with the item's fields. With `field`, the button is a toggle: pressed while that boolean field of the item is true, labelled `on_label` then, and fired with `on` set to the new value; the item is read again afterwards.

field.description: Dotted path to a boolean on the item.

busy_label.description: MUSIC-LIKE-01: the button's words and disabled state while its action runs (for a slow call such as making a band), so one press cannot start it twice.

visible_field.description: Boolean row field controlling visibility; defaults to can_edit.

reader.description: MEDIA-BOOKS-01: one bound book (an object or the first row), drawn by the kit Reader. Default fields: id, src (same-origin URL), title, format (epub or pdf), locator ({kind: cfi, cfi, spine_index?, block_index?} or {kind: page, page}, 1-based). Heavy engines load only when a book opens.

format.description: Override the bound format field; absent reads fields.format or format.

font_size.description: EPUB font step: 85, 100, 115, 130, 150, 175 or 200 percent. PDF ignores it.

fields.description: Dotted field paths overriding the default book fields; locator is the saved reader locator, for example position.locator.

on_locator.description: Debounced 250 ms after relocation, flushed on close, hide and unmount. Receives the item's fields plus {locator} (a JSON object) and {percent} (number, 0 to 100); nested placeholders such as {locator.cfi} work too. Quiet calls do not refetch the binding.

on_close.description: Draw Close and fire with the book's fields after flushing pending progress.

clip_feed.description: CLIPS-FEED-01: a full-screen vertical feed of the household's OWN short clips, one per screen (the kit's ClipFeed, composed from the shipped carousel in its vertical orientation and the VideoPlayer Element; no new player). `bind` is a package data call returning the clips as rows (the existing `clips` scope rows; nothing new is stored). The visible clip plays muted and loops (unless autoplay is off), the next one is preloaded and every other clip is only its poster. One tap pauses or plays; a mute button remembers the person's choice; a thin bar scrubs; a right-hand rail holds Like and Make another; the feed has its own Close button. Under prefers-reduced-motion, or when autoplay is off, nothing plays by itself: the poster and a Play button show. A clip file that cannot load falls back to its poster. `empty_state` is the status card for a feed with no clips.

item_fields.description: Dotted paths into each row. `src` and `poster` are same-origin paths; `duration_s` is seconds (a number); `liked` is a boolean.

actions.description: The rail. Each is one action (navigate, call or confirm) run with the row; an undeclared one draws no button. `like` also gets `{liked}` (the new boolean, typed) beside the row's own fields. `remake` (Make another) may carry the K8 `starts` marker; it defaults to `video`, so the host's `makingNotice` disables the button, with that notice beside it, while making is unavailable.

start_id.description: The id of the clip to open on. Absent or not found: the first clip.

on_close.description: Fired by the feed's always-visible Close button. Absent: Close goes back one page.

autoplay.description: False: nothing plays or advances by itself (poster and a Play button), the setting for a child band. Prefers-reduced-motion does the same whatever this says.

autoplay_field.description: Dotted path to a boolean on the first row; false turns autoplay off, so the data call can decide per person (a child band). Combined with `autoplay`: autoplay happens only when both allow it.

detail_pane.description: The kit's DetailPane primitive (frontend/src/kit/primitives/DetailPane.tsx): the 'one thing, in full' half of a SplitView. Not used by any page this session builds; added for catalog/schema completeness.

split_view.description: The kit's SplitView primitive (ui/src/primitives/SplitView.tsx). Two forms: `list` and `detail` (an index beside one item, taking turns on a phone), or MEDIA-POLISH-01's `main` and `aside` (a wide column with a narrow one beside it from the kit's desktop breakpoint `lg`, 960 px, stacked below that: a player with Up next). A package page may use the main and aside form.

aside_label.description: The aside column's accessible name ("Up next").

aside_sheet.description: On phone, hide the aside and open it in a Drawer from a labelled button. Not combined with a `prompt_bar` of `placement: "panel"` in the aside (the bar draws its own dock and sheet); checkAppPackage refuses the pair.

aside_side.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K11): the side the aside takes at `lg` and up. `start` puts it on the left (a control panel beside a results feed); `end` (default) is unchanged. Below `lg` the aside stacks under the main column as before.

aside_width.description: VIDEO-UI-12: the aside column's width at `lg` (960 px) and up. `default` is 360 px, unchanged; `wide` is 420 px (a roomy control panel). Below `lg` the aside stacks as before.

main_surface.description: VIDEO-UI-13: the surface the main column draws on. `page` (default) is unchanged: the column sits on the page. `stage` draws it as a recessed pane on the kit token `--surface-stage` (darker than the page in dark theme, a soft grey in light theme), the frame a feed of pictures and clips sits in. Tokens only: a colour never comes from the page. Only the main and aside form has it.

widget_card.description: Renders the actor's `size: "card"` widgets (D to E's `contributes.widgets[]` contract, docs/plans/wave-2.md) in a grid sized by the kit's card-size slider (frontend/src/kit/primitives/CardSizeSlider.tsx, 180-560px, per app per device). Not a `card_grid` bound straight to display rows: `bind` resolves to the widget list only (`GET /api/widgets`); each widget's own display data (`GET /api/widgets/:package/:id/data`) is a second, per-widget fetch the interpreter makes on that widget's own `refresh_s`, since the list route and the data route are two different calls by design (the list is cheap and shared, the data is per-package and cached server-side).

widget_row.description: The `size: "row"` counterpart to `widget_card`: same binding and per-widget data fetch, a slim horizontal row instead of a sized grid tile - no card-size slider applies (a row's height is fixed; only a grid of cards has a size to pick).

widget_tiles.description: MEDIA-PARITY-02: the `size: "tiles"` counterpart to `widget_card` and `widget_row`, for a device widget (lights, locks, sensors): the widget draws a compact grid of small device tiles, each one a name, a state and one tap action, filling one card-width cell of the page. Same binding and per-widget data fetch as `widget_card`; the widget's data is a list of {id, name, state, icon?, on?}.

answer_blocks.description: Draws the answer blocks a package data call returns (APP-KIND-02), each through the kit's one answer-block dispatcher (validation, then the kit Element named by `kind`; an unknown kind or invalid props shows the block's `alt` sentence). A page's hero is a first node of this type. `bind` is a package binding whose data call returns {blocks}.

kinds.description: Draw only blocks of these kinds, so a page can place one kind per section. Absent: every block returned.

filter_state.description: NEWS-LOOK-02: the page-state key the block's filter chips write when one is chosen (the chip's `id`; an empty id means All). The page's data call reads it back through `$state.<key>` in its bind params. Without it the chips are not drawn.

states.description: WEATHER-FIX-01: what the page says when its data call cannot draw blocks for a stated reason, in the page's own words. `needs_place`: the call answered {needs: "place"} (the person has no place chosen) or failed with code needs_place. `down`: the source could not be reached (code down). `timed_out`: it took too long (code timed_out). Any other empty or failed call keeps `empty_state` and the generic retry.

actions.description: NEWS-00: the actions a block may fire, by role. A block fires an entry with the item's own ids and never names a route itself. `open` navigates to a story and `open_channel` to a channel (the ids are `channel_kind` and `channel_key`), `save`, `follow`, `feedback` and `summarize` call, `reset_mix` asks first (`confirm`), `listen` plays, `discuss` navigates to the app's page that opens a chat about the story. A package page's entries stay under its own `/api/plugins/<id>/` and `/apps/<id>/` prefixes (spec/ui/app-check.ts).

data_state.description: A stated reason for an answer_blocks node with nothing to draw: an icon, an optional title, the sentence, and up to three buttons.

to.description: A screen of this app: /apps/<id>..., or its own settings area /settings/<id>.

state.description: The page-state name set to "current" with the device coordinates in `<state>_geo`, on this click only.

tabs.description: NEWS-00: peer views of one page (Topics and Sources, say), drawn by the kit's Tabs primitive. Peer views only: the shell owns navigation between pages (UI.md). The active tab is page state `state` (default: the first tab), mirrored in the URL by the shell.

picker.description: Chooses one value and writes it to page state (APP-KIND-02), drawn with the kit's select primitive. Fixed `leading` options come first, then the rows of `bind` (a package data call returning {rows}). A section's `condition` reads the state it writes.

variant.description: Pill reuses TabsList variant pill for leading options and bound rows (for example seasons), reading selection from page state and writing the chosen row key.

state.description: The page-state name this picker writes.

label.description: The accessible name of the control.

placeholder.description: Shown while nothing is chosen (for example "Default place").

needs.description: Choosing this option asks the browser for the device location, on that choice only. The coordinates stay in memory as page state `<state>_geo` ({lat, lon}); they are never stored.

prompt_bar.description: VIDEO-CREATE-01: a prompt box with chips and one Make button. Every chip and the optional tier segment write their chosen value to page state under their own `state` key as it changes; the prompt text is written under `prompt_state` when Make is pressed. Make fires `submit` once with the item {<prompt_state>: text, <each chip state>: value, <tier state>: id}, so `{prompt}` and `{shape}` placeholders in the call args fill from it (a whole-string placeholder keeps a number's type). Make stays off while the prompt is empty. The node sends nothing itself. VIDEO-CREATE-02 (additive): a chip may set `variant: "cards"` with an optional `media` per option, and an optional `references` list adds picture slots whose file ids join the item. VIDEO-UI-03 (additive): `placement: "panel"` draws the bar as a control panel when an enclosing `split_view` provides its mode. `layout: "composer"` groups prompt, references, controls, tier and submit inside one bordered input mechanism. `suggestions` are idea chips shown while the words are empty; `submit_detail` is the line under the submit; chips may set `presentation`, `group` and `fold`; a reference may set `placement: "in_field"` and its `kind` may be `audio` or `video`; `starts` lets the host disable only the submit with its availability reason while keeping the prompt and options editable.

media.description: VIDEO-CREATE-02: a relative package asset path to a short silent mp4 or webp loop, or an image (png, jpg, webp, svg). Used by the `cards` variant only; an option without it draws a plain tile with its label.

note.description: VIDEO-LORA-09: one plain line shown under the chip's cards while this option is chosen (what it does, and what it adds to the person's words). Plain text, never markup.

icon.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-03: optional compact Lucide icon name shown with this dropdown choice.

variant.description: VIDEO-CREATE-02: `cards` draws the options as a grid of picture cards (one choice, a radio group) instead of a dropdown. The value is written to page state under `state` exactly as a dropdown chip's is.

default.description: The option chosen first; the first option when omitted.

presentation.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K3a): `popover` shows the chip as one trigger (its chosen thumbnails and words) that opens its options in a popover, a sheet on a phone. Chips with the same `group` share one trigger. Inside a panel's bottom sheet the options are drawn flat, three to a row.

group.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K3a): the visible name of a shared popover trigger ("Style"). Chips with the same `group` open one popover; a text chip may be in the group.

fold.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K3b): list this chip under a collapsed "More settings" control.

trigger.description: VIDEO-UI-13: on a popover `group`, `banner` draws the shared trigger as a poster banner (the chosen card's picture, the group's chip names, the chosen words and a Change pill) instead of the small row. Read from the first chip of the group that sets it. Default unchanged.

popover_size.description: VIDEO-UI-13: on a popover `group`, `wide` opens a wider popover (about 760 px) with six cards a row and each card chip as its own section (tabs when the surface is below `lg`). Read from the first chip of the group that sets it. Default unchanged.

locked.description: VIDEO-LORA-09 (cards variant): adds the one lock tile to the chip's cards, standing for every choice the Adult lock hides (no name, no count). Pressing it opens the page's passcode dialog (`AdultLockProvider`); once unlocked, the host's page refetch returns the real cards and the tile is gone. Default unchanged.

enabled_tiers.description: VIDEO-LORA-09: the levels (the bar's `tier` segment) at which this chip can be used. At any other level the chip is drawn disabled, its choice is left out of the submit item, and `disabled_reason` is shown under its cards. Absent: usable at every level. Default unchanged.

disabled_reason.description: VIDEO-LORA-09: the one plain line shown under a chip's cards while the chip is disabled (with `enabled_tiers`, at a level it cannot use; without it, always disabled).

private.description: VIDEO-LORA-09: the chip's choice is never written into the page address (an id of an adult-only style must not reach a link, history or a shared URL). It stays in page state and in the submit item. Default unchanged.

quiet_value.description: VIDEO-LORA-09: while this value is chosen the chip adds nothing to the group's summary words and thumbnail row (a "No style" or "Normal" default). Default unchanged.

align.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-03: place this control at the leading or trailing side of a distributed chat toolbar.

icon_only.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-03: show the selected icon in the closed control without its text label; the accessible name and open choices keep their words.

mode_selector.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-03: a compact media kind selector in the Chat-style prompt toolbar.

mode_actions.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-03: submit action overrides by mode value; modes without an override use `submit`.

references.description: VIDEO-CREATE-02: dashed square slots under the prompt box. Each takes one picture chosen through the host's media picker, shows it as a thumbnail with a remove control, and writes the chosen file id under `state` (in page state and in the submit item); an empty slot is absent from the item.

kind.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K4): `audio` and `video` slots take a voice clip or a source clip through the host's media picker.

placement.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K3c): `in_field` shows the chosen file inside the prompt box as a named thumbnail with a remove control. At most one slot, a `picture`, `character` or `place`. VIDEO-UI-12: `tile` draws a full-width dashed tile (an icon, the label and a one-line hint) in the box; once a file is chosen it shows as the named thumbnail with a remove control, as `in_field` does. At most one `in_field` or `tile` slot between them, a `picture`, `character` or `place`.

hint.description: VIDEO-UI-12: the one line under the label on a `tile` slot ("Optional. Begin from a picture."). Ignored by the other placements.

tier.description: The kit tier segment (Standard, Boost, Max).

presentation.description: VIDEO-UI-12: `segment` (default) is the pill segment with one hint line. `cards` draws one card per level. `dropdown` uses the compact chat answer-style control, with one plain benefit line per choice.

placement.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K2a): `inline` (default) is a block in the page flow, unchanged. `panel` is a control panel beside a feed: it needs an enclosing `split_view` (main and aside form) and reads that split_view's layout, side by side at `lg` (960 px) and up, stacked below. Outside a `split_view` it draws as `inline`.

layout.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-02/03: `chat` adapts Home's compact Chat composer to a prompt field with reference attachment, compact option controls and a round submit action in one toolbar; `chat_distribution` places compact choices at opposite ends of its toolbar; `composer` is the earlier grouped layout; `block` preserves the original stacked layout.

chat_distribution.description: VIDEO-COMPOSER-03: distribute compact chat composer controls between start and end of its toolbar.

field_size.description: VIDEO-UI-12: the prompt box's height. `default` is unchanged; `large` is about 140 px tall (5 rows) in the panel and the inline bar, and unchanged in the phone dock.

suggestions.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K2b): idea chips shown while the words are empty; pressing one puts its `text` in the box.

submit_detail.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K2c): the small line under the submit button, chosen by the current value of one chip or the tier (`state` names its key); a value with no entry shows no line. Say time, never credits.

placement.description: VIDEO-UI-12: `below` (default) is the line under the button, unchanged. `in_button` draws the time as the second line inside the submit button (a taller, 64 px full-width button).

style_suggest.description: STYLES-04: up to `max` removable suggested-style chips under the prompt. `rows` is a package binding (source `package`) whose rows are {id, name, kind: "style" | "character"}; its `params` may read the prompt with "$state.<prompt_state>" (the bar's current text is supplied). The bar asks about 500 ms after typing stops, only with 3 or more characters, and ignores out-of-date or failed answers. A chip showing is ON: Make sends its id under `style_state` (kind style, default `style`) or `character_state` (kind character, default `character`), unless the person already chose a value for that key by hand, in which case no chip shows for that kind. Removing a chip sends nothing and it does not return for that prompt. Those two keys are private (never in the address).

starts.description: VIDEO-UI-03 (K8): the submit starts a picture or a clip. The host's `makingNotice(kind)`, when it has one and returns a line, disables only the submit and shows the reason; the prompt and options stay editable. No marker: unchanged.

search.description: NEWS-LOOK-02: a search field that writes what is typed to page state (debounced) and, on Enter, fires `submit` with the item {q}, so `{q}` placeholders in a navigate state or call args fill from it. With `recents` bound and the field empty it draws the rows as chips (a chip sets the state key to its label and fires `submit`); `clear_recents` fires from a Clear button. The node sends nothing itself.

state.description: The page-state key the typed text is written to.

item_key_field.description: The recents row's key field. Default `key`.

item_label_field.description: The recents row's label field. Default `label`.

suggest.description: MEDIA-PARITY-02: search suggestions. While the field has at least `min_chars` characters the kit asks `bind` (a package data call; put `$state.<state>` in its params to read the typed text) about 250 ms after typing stops, ignores out-of-date or failed answers, and draws the rows under the field. Pressing a row sets the state key to its label and fires `submit`. With the field empty, `recents` is drawn as before.

item_key_field.description: The suggestion row's key field. Default `key`.

item_label_field.description: The suggestion row's label field. Default `label`.

type_chips.description: PARITY-01: type chips under the field (All, Songs, Artists, Albums). The chosen `value` is written to page state `state`; sections below use `condition` on that key to show only the matching shelves. The first option is the default.

nav_entry.description: One row in the shell's nav (docs/plans/session-b-ui.md step 2, frontend/src/shell/nav.ts). Not part of the root `oneOf` above: a nav entry is never a page-body node a page's `body`/`children` array renders - it describes the shell's own chrome, the same distinction `page` (a route) already draws from `section`/`form` (page content). A package's manifest `contributes.pages[]` entry emits this shape minus `to` (design-resolver, 2026-09-06, docs/BACKLOG.md's `app`-kind item): `icon` and `label` carry over as-is, and the shell derives `to` from the package and page ids (`/apps/<package id>/<page id>`) rather than trusting a package to name its own route. Core's own pages still declare this shape by hand in nav.ts today.

to.description: A route path, matching a `page.id`'s route.
